lines.en: : Fucking hippocampus. Fucking norepinephrine. Fucking pre-frontal cortex and fucking REM and fucking stupid fucking bathtub.
: If I could just remember what happens in my sleep, I could be rid of these blasted headaches once and for all. But alas — I must suffer. I must raise the water bill.
: One woe doth tread upon another’s heel! So fast they follow. Your sister’s drowned, Laertes!
: There is a willow grows askant the brook that shows his hoar leaves in the glassy stream.
: Therewith fantastic garlands did she make of crowflowers, nettles, daisies, and long purples that liberal shepherds give a grosser name...but our cold maids do “dead men’s fingers” call them...

: Fuck you, Shakespeare. Fuck you, Laertes. This body belongs not to Ophelia nor Hamlet, but me. And shall I be swallowed by the waves of these perpetual days, be it known that my passing is involuntary.
: Sound the bells nestled in their rocky dwellings. Let their cries recant my disappearance and carry my ashes once more over beds of blue hydrangeas, pruned by men of lesser color.
: I have completed my mandatory reunion with hygiene! Too much of water hast I! Poor Nodoka! Terrible Nodoka! This woman is out! Adieu, my lord! Adieu!
: Let’s follow Gertrude!
: I’m doing fine. Thank you for asking.
: I must return to the dorms tonight. Remaining here any longer will only drive me deeper into madness.
: There’s news, though.
: Rejoice. The world is broken.
: And while that isn’t that grand of a surprise, something else is.
: I’m not the only one who knows it.
: I’ve stumbled into someone else’s party without an invitation. Is this how it feels to be popular?
: Don’t answer that. I know you were about to.
: You’re so full of life these days. Chatting up a storm. A tempest, even. Preventing me from leaving. Sleeping.
: Oh, the things I’d do for silence. To feel at peace even once.
: Kyoko...
: What am I?
: What would become of you if I were to stop showing up one day?
: Humans can only last up to a week without water.  But does such a word even apply to us?
: Are we really human if we can not die? If we were never born?
: Would you die? Were you born?
: And, if you won’t die, how long would you stay in that chair? Staring at that screen.
: I sometimes wish my world was as small as yours.
: That someone would bathe me. Feed me. Protect me.
: Hug me.
: I don’t intend to burden you with such intimate contact.
: But I think about it sometimes.
: And we can discuss if such a thing would be acceptable or not once you wake up.
: I’m getting closer. I can feel it.
: Do you even want to wake up, though?
: Does this make me selfish, I wonder?
: I enjoyed this conversation. But I apologize that I was naked for it.
: Good morning, Mr. Blake. Or shall I say good evening? Could I trouble you for the time in exchange for this bit of bread?
: Nodoka! Nodoka! Scrawk! Happy! Happy! Scrawk!
: Are you truly happy, Mr. Blake? I can’t imagine it’s enjoyable living inside of a cabinet like this. Animal control would surely seize you if they knew.
: Scrawk! Happy! Happy! A gift for God! A gift for God!
: Now now, Mr. Blake. If I give you this bread, you need to promise not to use it as a tribute to the deity of your choice. This is an atheist household, I’ll have you know.
: Scraaaawk! Shiori-chan! Shiori-chan! Scraaaaawk!
: Kyoko doesn’t like it when you use that name.
: You best watch your tongue or you’ll wind up in our next hot pot, Mr. Blake.
: Scrawwwk! Scrawk! Sorry! Scrawk! Very sorry!
: An apology is unnecessary. I’ll bring you better food tomorrow. I didn’t realize we were out.
: Would you like to sit on her shoulder? Do you promise to walk yourself home if I let you out?
: Promise! Scrawk! Happy! Happy!
: Kyoko, Mr. Blake would like to see you. Are you accepting visitors at the moment?
: Scrawk! Scraaaaaawk!
: I’m sorry, Mr. Blake. If you haven’t noticed, Kyoko is rather busy at the moment and isn’t accepting company.
: SCRAWWWK! Scraaaawk! Sacrifice! Sacrifice!
: Okay, okay. There’s no need to make any sacrifices either.
: Here. Have at her. Can you pluck her feathers in my absence? The way I do yours?
: Where going? Scraaawk! Where going?
: I won’t be long.
: It’s just the other side of the weeping brook...
Nodoka Nagasawa was used to the dark.
In fact, she found it easier to apply her makeup that way.
Kyoko reacted to the lights, so they weren’t used often.
Not much here was used often.
It was mainly just a computer. A hot plate. The water.
Even the outlet beside the cot where Nodoka slept on visits was a virgin.
She didn’t use her phone here. Kyoko reacted to that too.
All of these “reactions” were subtle, though.
So subtle that the laymen like you would never pick up on them.
A daughter could, though.
A “daughter” could.
: I’m stealing some of your clothes. I didn’t bring any extras with me this time.
: Take care.
: I will see you soon.
Even disregarding who she was and how she got here, Nodoka Nagasawa was an interesting specimen.
Drifting back and forth between the public eye and what I’ve come to know as the eyelid that shields us from worlds unseen, she was both two people at once and also no one at all.

This sort of thing would be difficult for anyone else. But considering she was none of them and all of them, two lives weren’t that hard to balance. And there was no reason to really merge them either.
Kyoko would be kept a secret. It was safer for her that way. And it was easier for Nodoka as well because dealing with “sympathy” was never something she was good at.
She was good at sponge baths, though. Helping people chew their food. Changing their clothes and brushing their hair.
Making sure they always looked as pretty as they were described by their peers in old notebooks that faded in and out of existence whenever they weren’t being looked at.
And as she marched down a road she could see with her eyes closed, she hoped the same was true of her mother.
That, in leaving, Nodoka was doing her a favor and suspending her existence somewhere between whatever it was she experienced so many years ago and all she struggles to experience today.
She had never heard her voice. She had never felt her embrace. And she had never seen her stand.

Everything Nodoka had ever learned about her mother was something someone else learned first — so the entire concept of “family” was something essentially passed down through an endless game of telephone.

It’d be easy to just abandon her. To falsify some tragic tale ending with her passing and move on to realizing the ambitions everyone assumes she has when what she really wants is far more simple than that.
This creature cared not for gods or their angels. For contracts or constructs like time or language. Those were all just monsters she was forced to wrestle on the way back home.
It was a long, depressing journey though. And one that seemed even longer all of a sudden now that the monsters were evolving and adapting to this sick place we’ve found ourselves in.
This infinite emptiness, this unending struggle where self battles seraphim was naught but the residue  of prior collapses bubbling up until we’re all worried it will trigger the smoke alarms.
The unfortunate truth that serves as the jacket for the infinite emptiness is that the alarms are already blaring, though.
Too many anomalies had found themselves here for one reason or another. And Nodoka was special, yes. But she wasn’t the only one special anymore. And that made things complicated.
Were these mysteries connected? Or was each iteration of exaggerated misery its own language?
It was all getting so tiring. Learning. Thinking. Being. And while it seemed like such a place would be a playground for her, it was anything but.

It was more like she was packed into the waiting room of an urgent care facility with a loved one bleeding out in her lap, forced to wait until her last name is shouted across a sea of separate dying onlookers.
Nodoka was good with her hands. She understood anatomy and medical science better than most nurses. So why would she wait here instead of just fixing the issue herself?
She couldn’t come up with a reason. She couldn’t care.
But she had never been good at that to begin with. And she didn’t care about caring either. At least most of the time.
It was only when she was distracted that her judgment would lapse and she’d deceive herself into thinking she’s anything more than a ghost walking in the shadows of its prior self.
Those old boots fit perfectly. But even then, she couldn’t fathom even fathoming how Kyoko walked in them. The friends she made and the struggles she endured.
And oh, were there struggles.
Refocus. Rethink. Rewrite. Redo. Repair.
Pay no mind to these distractions — to these monsters knocking at your door and remember why you are here, Nodoka.
Remember why I am here.
She arrives back home. And when she does, everything looks just as grey as always.

Scuff marks on the wooden floor from where Otoha would rock her chair back and forth to help her think. Coffee rings on stacks of research papers. Bits of wood from a dead tree that somehow kept on dying.
The faint hum of an old computer monitor was missing, though. Scratching from within a kitchen cabinet. Harsher scratching in a closeted litter box.
Somewhere down the line, those things became music to her.
: Holy shit. You’re actually alive.
And while she rarely grew tired of listening to them on repeat, she liked these sounds too. These sounds of a separate world.
That was just it, though. A separate world.
Another piece of the puzzle that she wouldn’t think thrice of before slotting it into its designated resting place.
She’d think twice, though. And it wasn’t always that way.
She was changing, whether she accepted it or not.
She was weakening.
Just like the world itself.
: Where the fuck have you been? And what makes you think you’re allowed to be so hot all of a sudden?
: You like the new outfit? I wore it just for you.
: Well, it’d work if I knew literally nothing else about you. Now, what the hell’s going on? Did you throw your phone off of a cliff or something?
: I climbed into a rabbit hole and woke up in a strange, fantastical world. Had I known you’d miss me this much, I’d have offered to take you with me.
: Must’ve been a big fucking rabbit hole if you’ve been gone for an entire week.
: Come again?

: Is everything okay? Like, I figured you were having another one of your episodes, but to just straight up vanish for a week without so much as answering my calls and telling me to eat a dick was weird for even you.
: I’ve been gone for a week?

: Yes, dude. I had to tell Imani you were on some sort of fucking book tour and now she knows you’re legit and is probably going to read your stupid Kumon-mi High fan-fic and subsequently ruin Akira’s entire harem.
: Fascinating. An entire week. And you didn’t think to come look for me?
: Where would I look? I don’t know your home address.
: Futaba does. I think. Did she come looking for me?
: Apparently not if that’s where you were. Was it?
: It’s where I was today. I can’t speak for the other six days I was apparently missing, though.
: So you were zoned out for all of them? And now you’re suddenly a hot goth girl? There’s no way that’s normal.
: You were kidnapped and brainwashed. Then probably released because you annoyed them or something. It’s the only logical explanation I can think of if you don’t have anything.
: Otoha, do you ever remember your dreams?
: Only the sexual ones.
: Mm...no. That’s not what I’m looking for.
: You can still tell me about them if you want, though.
: I don’t.
: No, really. It’s okay.
: No. It’s not.
: How unfortunate. I imagine practically anything would arouse me right now if it’s truly been a week since I vanished.
: I feel like you are way less concerned about this than you should be. Like, if I vanished for a week, I’d be freaking the fuck out right now.
: Did Akira ever come by?
: Uhh...once. Why?
: For me?
: Again, why?
: Just taking inventory on who is concerned about me. It may come in handy later.
: What, you mean the next time you disappear for a week? Want to give me your address so I can come chase after you or something?
: Otoha, are we friends?
: Uhh...yeah?
: Why?
: Why...are we friends? Because we...I don’t know. We just are?
: Even when we don’t know anything about each other?
: You’re being weird as fuck right now.
: I’m sorry. I didn’t realize it was a difficult question.
: Listen, just...either give me your address or we can link our phones together so I can track you the next time you go missing.
: I didn’t want to start keeping tabs on you like Touka does with Yasu, but maybe Akira was right about you needing something like that even more than she does. I worry about you, Nodoka.
: Why? I’m fine. And, upon further reflection, I don’t like the idea of you following me down the rabbit hole.
: Nodoka-
: Please excuse me. I have no idea when the last time I ate was.
: Nodo- oh, come on!
: I’m hungry too! But you’re gonna make me look like shit if I have to go out with you while you’re dressed like that!
: I will tear the outfit in two so we can share. Would you like the top half, or the bottom?
: Neither! Just...keep them both to yourself!
In the many documented worlds unseen, there are few I have the time to show you.
This is not malicious on my end. Nor is it something I’m refusing for the sake of maintaining a thin layer of mystique.
I just think there’s something special to be found in this one.
A home for anomalies. For dreams and things like us.
And if you think this home does not suit you, that’s fine.
If you’ve made it here, you’re always welcome.
These doors will never close.
Also, I am a liar.
Nodoka’s affection has increased to [nodoka_love]!
